hymn: Holy, Holy, Holy
notes: Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 (Wikisource) stanza 1; Cyber line breaks are short lines

hymn: Break Thou the Bread of Life
author_as_printed: Mary Lathbury, 1877, and Alexander Groves, 1913 (Cyber credit; stanza 1 is Lathbury)
notes: Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 stanza 1 (whose Wikisource transcription has typo "Dear lord")

hymn: Watchman, Tell Us of the Night
notes: Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 has "doth" (Cyber Hymnal modernises to "does"). Stanza is 8 lines. Cyber: http://www.hymntime.com/tch/htm/w/a/t/c/watchman.htm

hymn: Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted
notes: SINGLE SOURCE (no second text found). Cyber Hymnal dates it 1804, brief says 1809; Kelly d. 1855. Stanza is 8 lines (two quatrains)

hymn: Dies Iræ (Irons translation)
author_as_printed: Tommaso da Celano, tr. William Josiah Irons, 1849
notes: Stanza 1 is 3 lines as printed (Irons 1849 reading "once more the Cross returning"; Cyber Hymnal prints a hymnal-revised "See fulfilled the prophet's warning"). Opening printed in capitals "DAY"

hymn: Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing
stanza: 4 of 5 (the "O to grace how great a debtor" stanza)
notes: Third line "Let Thy goodness, like a fetter" is the 1758 wording; Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 prints later variant "Let that grace now, like a fetter" (and OCR "0 to grace")

hymn: Rock of Ages
notes: Toplady wording ("From Thy wounded side... Save from wrath and make me pure"). Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 prints Hastings-era variant ("riven side... Cleanse me from its guilt and power"). Title in Cyber is "Rock of Ages"; first line "Rock of Ages, cleft for me"

hymn: O for a Heart to Praise My God
notes: SINGLE SOURCE printing of 1742 wording ("blood so freely spilt"). The Wikisource page of this hymn is a modernised version ("shed"), not used

hymn: Be Still, My Soul
author_as_printed: Katharina von Schlegel, 1752; tr. Jane L. Borthwick, 1855 (Hymns from the Land of Luther)
notes: SINGLE SOURCE. Stanza is 6 lines. Hymnary.org representative text (Psalter Hymnal) is modernised "your" and not used

hymn: Dear Lord and Father of Mankind (from "The Brewing of Soma")
notes: Whittier text (also Cyber Hymnal http://www.hymntime.com/tch/htm/d/e/a/r/dearlord.htm). The Canadian Soldiers' Song Book (Wikisource rev 7246235) prints the hymnal adaptation "Forgive our feverish ways! / Re-clothe us": use that only if editors want the hymnal form. The hymn is an extract of a longer poem

hymn: Jesus, Lover of My Soul
notes: Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 keeps Wesley "be past"; Cyber Hymnal reads "is past" and Savior. Cyber: http://www.hymntime.com/tch/htm/j/l/m/y/jlmysoul.htm

hymn: O God, Our Help in Ages Past
notes: Cyber page opens "Our God, our help in ages past" (title in list says "O God"); wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920

hymn: Just as I Am, Without One Plea
notes: Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 stanza 1

hymn: O Love That Wilt Not Let Me Go
notes: Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 except its "will not" in title/first line; Cyber "wilt" is Matheson wording

hymn: Judge Eternal, Throned in Splendor
notes: SINGLE SOURCE. Holland d. 1918, text published 1902: public domain in US. Stanza is 6 lines. Not in Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 (Wikisource) under this title

hymn: Where Cross the Crowded Ways of Life
notes: North published 1903 (US public domain; d. 1935). CHECK LINE 4: Army and Navy transcription lacks "O" before "Son of man"; Cyber (http://www.hymntime.com/tch/htm/w/h/e/r/e/wherecro.htm) reads "We hear your voice, O Son of Man" (modernised "your"). Editors should confirm "O" against the original 1903 text

hymn: Come, Ye Sinners, Poor and Needy
notes: SINGLE SOURCE

hymn: Abide with Me (Lyte)
notes: Lyte original wording "The darkness thickens" (Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 prints altered "deepens"). Cyber breaks lines into short lines

hymn: Eternal Father, Strong to Save
notes: Whiting wording "hath bound"; Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 prints altered "doth bind"

hymn: Jesus, Savior, Pilot Me
notes: Matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 except spelling Saviour and its typo "shaol"

hymn: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God
author_as_printed: Martin Luther, 1529; tr. Frederic H. Hedge, 1853
notes: Stanza 3 wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 (its stanza 3 ends "His truth to triumph through us." and continues with the rest of the stanza)

hymn: Guide Me, O Thou Great Jehovah
notes: Editorial bracket line "[or Guide me, O Thou great Redeemer...]" removed; chorus lines "Bread of Heaven" are part of stanza 1 as printed. Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920

hymn: My Faith Looks Up to Thee
notes: Army and Navy header prints Ray Palmer, 1830. Wording matches Cyber Hymnal (http://www.hymntime.com/tch/htm/m/y/f/l/myfluptt.htm) apart from Saviour

hymn: Rescue the Perishing
notes: Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 stanza 1; refrain not included

hymn: The King of Love My Shepherd Is
notes: Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 (whose transcription has syllable hyphens)

hymn: I to the Hills Will Lift Mine Eyes (Psalm 121)
notes: Cyber Hymnal "I to the Hills Will Lift My Eyes" is the 1912 Psalter revision ("O whence shall come my aid?") and was NOT used. Edition label on page: "1650 Scottish Psalter". Only one fetch, not cross-checked

hymn: Breathe on Me, Breath of God
notes: SINGLE SOURCE. Hatch d. 1889

hymn: Come, Holy Spirit, Heavenly Dove
notes: SINGLE SOURCE

hymn: Fight the Good Fight with All Thy Might
notes: Wording matches The Canadian Soldiers' Song Book (Wikisource rev 7246389) stanza 1

hymn: Glorious Things of Thee Are Spoken
notes: Matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 except "Formed" vs "Form'd"

hymn: Come, Thou Long Expected Jesus
notes: Wording matches Wikisource page "Come, Thou Long-Expected Jesus" (rev 15278608; source unknown there). Cyber lists 2 stanzas only

hymn: Crown Him with Many Crowns
author_as_printed: Matthew Bridges, 1852, and Godfrey Thring, 1874 (Cyber credit; stanza 1 is Bridges)
notes: Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 (heavenly/Thro' spelling differences)

hymn: Shall We Gather at the River?
notes: Matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 except "for ever"/"forever"; refrain not included

hymn: Jerusalem the Golden
author_as_printed: Bernard of Morlaix, 1146; tr. John M. Neale, 1858 (The Rhythm of Bernard of Morlaix)
notes: Author printed as Bernard of Morlaix (= of Cluny). Wording matches Army and Navy Hymnal 1920 stanza 1
